title: The Earliest Moment When Everyone Become Friends
statement:
A social network has `n` users, numbered `0` to `n - 1`. You are given `m` log entries. Entry `t a b` records that users `a` and `b` became friends at time `t`.

Friendship links users into groups: two users are **connected** if they are friends, or if there is a chain of friendships leading from one to the other (a friend of a friend of a friend, and so on). Once a friendship is formed it is never removed.

Find the **earliest time** at which every user is connected to every other user. If that never happens, even after all log entries, output `-1`.

Notes:

- The log entries are **not** necessarily given in chronological order.
- Several entries may share the same timestamp, and the same pair of users may appear in more than one entry.
- All friendships recorded at time `t` count as formed at time `t`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `m`: the number of users and the number of log entries.
Each of the next `m` lines contains three integers `t`, `a` and `b`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the earliest time at which all `n` users are connected, or `-1` if they never are.
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < n and a ≠ b

examples.explanation: Sorted by time: at 5 users 2 and 3 join, giving groups {0}, {1}, {2, 3}. At 12, 0 and 1 join: {0, 1}, {2, 3}. The entry at 20 links 0 and 1 again, which changes nothing. At 31, 1 and 2 become friends, merging everything into one group, so the answer is 31.
User 2 never appears in any log entry, so it is never connected to the others.
At time 3 only users 0 and 1 are connected. Both entries at time 7 then bring user 2 in, so all three are connected at 7.

hints: Process the log entries in increasing order of time; the answer is the timestamp of the entry that first leaves a single group.
Keep the groups in a disjoint-set union (union-find). Start with n groups and decrease the count whenever a union actually merges two different groups.
Use path compression (and optionally union by size) so each find runs in near-constant amortised time.
